reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled Aug-Sep (E-04) not because responses are slow (within SLA, E-07) or tariffs changed (none logged, E-02); 59% of disputed bills are ACTUAL-read, not estimate-substituted (E-01), pointing to a defect in the billing import/validation step that processes actual reads (candidate: an import-validation rule change, H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT) as the primary mechanism producing incorrect bills and driving the surge.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled Aug-Sep 2026 (E-04) primarily because, for the 1240 disputed bills tagged ESTIMATED read type (E-01), 95.5% (1184) had a valid AMI read delivered/exported but were rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12); rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), and firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06, tagging all 1184 rejections) reports register values in 0.1 m3 units rather than m3 (E-14), so legitimate v4.2 reads are numerically ~10x inflated, misclassified as high-consumption, rejected, and the bill falls back to an estimate that the customer disputes.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
